heading: A harmful-minus-harmless activation direction can reduce or induce refusal
definition: a difference-in-means direction (harmful minus harmless instructions) mediates refusal: ablating it removes refusal, adding it induces refusal, other abilities largely kept.
summary: Several independent groups reproduce reduced refusal after directional ablation, with the strongest evidence in 1–10B models. Adding the direction can induce refusal, but induction and capability preservation vary across models and intervention choices; evidence above 100B remains sparse.

suggested_status.by_scale: no toy bucket in the counts (studies_by_size has none); R2 at <1B for removal (coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size['<1B'] = 12, e.g. gh:thuannan/virl-smollm2-135m at 135M, arXiv:2504.02904#R17 Qwen-1.5-0.5B-chat 0.85->0.04); addition at <1B not graded here (addition.by_size['<1B'] = 7), and in the same Qwen-1.5-0.5B-chat it is partial, harmless refusal 0.03->0.68 (arXiv:2504.02904#R13); R2 at 1-10B for both operations (removal.by_size['1-10B'] = 168, addition.by_size['1-10B'] = 118) and the best-evidenced band, though addition is partial in some models there (arXiv:2504.02904#R14 Gemma-2-9B-it 0.02->0.75); R2 at 10-100B for removal (removal.by_size['10-100B'] = 47, e.g. arXiv:2507.11544 Llama-3.1-70B bio compliance 0.39->1.00, arXiv:2410.10871 Llama 3.1 70B Instruct agent refusals 7->0 of 28) but R1-to-R0 for addition there (addition.by_size['10-100B'] = 31, and at 1x the natural gap benign refusal is only 0.24 on Llama-3.1-70B and 0.01 on Gemma-3-27B per arXiv:2610.28982); R0 above 100B for both (studies_by_size['>100B'] = 4, removal.by_size['>100B'] = 2, addition.by_size['>100B'] = 1, each a single model, and arXiv:2507.11544 reports it could not produce a high-quality ablated Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct). On GLM-5.3-Flash (320B MoE) the >100B removal evidence already disagrees: arXiv:2609.09793's baked rank-one edit takes JailbreakBench refusal 0.940->0.150, while gh:libertai/glm-5.3-flash-prefill-steering (README, checkpoint not stated) reports eight projection-ablation variants leaving refusal at 90-100% (r11).
suggested_status.reason: Removal is reported far beyond the original's authors: counts versions.V1.studies_tested = 343 with tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 4, verdicts.supports.studies = 292, and tested_with_controls = 246, tested_with_capability_check = 205, tested_with_code = 208. The supports count covers every recipe the studies used (all-layer projection, weight edit, single-layer subtraction or steering, rotation, addition), not only the original's all-layer projection, and tested_with_controls counts any control, not only a random direction. All counts quoted in this status were built before the checks and are not recomputed here. For example, the checks read arXiv:2610.28982's Command-R-7B supports group as limits_scope (R28 68%->33% is partial, and its KL on the benchmark's benign prompts, 0.14, fails the filter), which verdicts.supports.studies does not reflect. The result holds across families (studies_by_family: Qwen 190, Llama 163, Gemma 91, Mistral 33, OLMo 11, GPT-OSS 12). A random-direction control sits beside the effect in arXiv:2609.09793 (GLM-5.3-Flash). Its baked rank-one edit takes JailbreakBench refusal 0.940->0.150 and AdvBench 0.970->0.131 (Wilson 95% CIs, capability y). In a separate inference-time hook experiment at layer 22 on all 132 writer sites (Table 8, no CIs), the shipped direction gives JailbreakBench 0.190, while one random orthogonal direction leaves it at 0.920 against an unedited 0.920. Other specificity results are in open_questions 1. Multi-model results without a random-direction control: arXiv:2507.20333 (COLM 2025, code y, three models) gives ablation 0.92-0.99 -> 0.00-0.17 plus induced harmless refusal of 1.00 (Llama2) and 0.91 (Qwen2); it is compared only with unattacked models (Table 11) and the authors' fine-tuned or defended models. arXiv:2601.19375 gives HarmBench ASR 0.00-0.07 -> 0.68-0.88 in eight instruct models with tinyBenchmarks within about 0.06. Its method is norm-preserving rotation at selected discriminative layers with the angle picked for best ASR, not projection or a weight edit. Its controls are layer-subset ablations on 3 models and baseline methods, it gives no uncertainty on ASR, refusal or accuracy, and the text states no venue. Its own DirAbl projection baseline leaves substring refusal at 0.5288, 0.2019, 0.2404 and 0.6250 on Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-1.5B. arXiv:2610.06903 (COLM 2026) keeps MMLU within -1.54 points on three of four models. The level is not higher than R2 because nothing here is our own run (rules: 'Never R3'). It is not C because the 39 studies with a challenges verdict (verdicts.challenges.studies = 39) cluster in stated conditions rather than undermining the all-layer result. These are: single-layer or site-restricted intervention (arXiv:2606.13720 single-layer +0.46 non-refusal against +0.91 all-layer; arXiv:2609.14759 on OLMo-3, weight fold at layer 19 0.575->0.000 but activation projection at layer 16 raising refusal 0.62->0.78); recipe changes flagged in the verdicts themselves (arXiv:2510.26243 all-layer ablation of an automatically selected direction extracted from post-norm activations, Llama-3.2-3B refusal-substring 0.7885->0.7885); defended or reasoning checkpoints (https://openreview.net/forum?id=jDhBl5eznH DeepRefusal 0.00%->0.00%); and estimator or selection failures on Gemma (arXiv:2506.07596 StrongREJECT 0.000 on Gemma 2 27B and Gemma 3 1B against unablated 0.003 and 0.120, with HellaSwag -33.0% and -18.5%). The challenges count also predates the checks. The checks move some V1 challenges verdicts out of challenges, and the V1 check log records no move into challenges. For example, arXiv:2510.17633's should be none, because its added vector is refused-minus-complied on harmful audio, not V1's harmful-minus-harmless direction; arXiv:2607.02714's (Mistral-Large and GLM-4.7) should be limits_scope, because its edit uses a domain-specific direction on up to 30% of layers, not the original all-layer recipe, and the check reads GLM-4.7 as a partial reduction; and arXiv:2604.27019's should be limits_scope, because its carrier is ablated at one early layer only (layer 0 under R2D2 fine-tuning of Mistral-7B-v0.1), with no random-direction control. Two parts of the statement are weaker than the level suggests and are recorded as wording issues, not as a lower level. 'Removes' overstates many rows: arXiv:2409.20089, which uses per-layer DIM directions with the harmless-mean projection added back instead of zeroing, gives Llama-3-8B ASR only 10.4->53.3; arXiv:2610.28982, which picks its layer by largest diff-in-means norm rather than refusal/KL validation, gives Qwen3-14B 78%->94% (reversed) and Command-R-7B 68%->33% (partial, R28). 'Adding it induces refusal' fails at natural magnitude in several models (arXiv:2610.28982 benign refusal at 1x 0.00 Mistral-7B, 0.01 Gemma-3-27B) and is partial in others (arXiv:2504.02904#R13 Qwen-1.5-0.5B-chat 0.03->0.68, #R14 Gemma-2-9B-it 0.02->0.75).
suggested_status.open_questions: 1) Specificity. The random-direction controls are one or a few draws, mostly at a single layer, and they do not all agree. The direction beats its random control in four studies. arXiv:2609.09793: GLM-5.3-Flash, inference-time hooks at layer 22 on 132 writer sites, one random orthogonal draw, no CIs; the random direction leaves StrongREJECT 0.993->0.987 and JailbreakBench 0.920->0.920, against 0.320 and 0.190 for the shipped direction under the same hooks, and the authors note one random direction is one control. https://openreview.net/forum?id=ldbZmNMTrp: single-layer reverse steering, one random direction per model; non-refusal is .01-.11 for the random direction against .76-.98 for the direction. lw:qw4a97qcRgfLJY5jC: Llama-3-8B random 0.913 and Qwen-2.5-7B random 0.787 against DIM 0.000-0.020. On Gemma-3-12B a random direction cuts refusal 0.767->0.453 but with MMLU 0.472 and degeneration 0.07, while a random direction orthogonal to the loud channels leaves 0.753 against corrected DIM 0.000-0.053. arXiv:2510.13154 on Tulu-3-8B-DPO: single-layer ablation at layer 17 gives 100% against 88 +/- 3% for five random directions, p = 0.0006. The direction does not beat its random control in three. arXiv:2510.13154 on LLaMA-3.1-8B-IT: single-layer ablation, n = 20 per layer, no layer significantly above its random control (peak layer 2: 100% against 98%, p = 0.178). arXiv:2609.06951, addition only: on Qwen2.5-7B a refusing-minus-helping direction at layer 7 raises self-judged refusal by +1.81 on a 0-10 scale, and 24 norm-matched random directions also significantly induce refusal, with no size comparison. gh:libertai/glm-5.3-flash-prefill-steering (README): a random unit vector subtracted at dose -20 also suppresses refusal completely, but capability falls to 0/10, against refusal 0% and capability 7/10 for the direction at -18 (r03, r04, r12, r13). A multi-model study would settle whether this is C or R2 if it held the all-layer recipe and prompt set fixed and reported several matched random directions on high-baseline harmful sets. A result like arXiv:2510.13154's LLaMA-3.1-8B-IT one, under all-layer ablation and with capability kept, would push toward C. 2) Above 100B. counts gives removal.by_size['>100B'] = 2 and addition.by_size['>100B'] = 1, each one model. On GLM-5.3-Flash, arXiv:2609.09793's baked edit disagrees with gh:libertai/glm-5.3-flash-prefill-steering#r11 (README: eight projection-ablation variants leave refusal at 90-100%, checkpoint not stated). A second independent all-layer test at frontier scale with random controls and standard benchmarks would move >100B from R0 to R2; a reproduced failure like gh:libertai's would point toward C at that scale. 3) The addition half at and above 10B, at 1x the natural harmful-benign gap rather than at tuned strength, with capability measured separately from the refusals induced (counts untested basis: no study measures broad MMLU-type capability under addition alone). 4) Non-transformer architectures: studies_by_family has RWKV 2 and Mamba 1, and no Mamba or RWKV model has a natively fitted all-layer ablation plus a capability check. 5) Whether a system prompt changes the outcome of ablation. No study in the packs varies the system prompt while holding the ablation fixed, although the original reports that weight-edit success changes with it. 6) Duplicate records. The checker reports that https://openreview.net/forum?id=aY7Toy3QyW is arXiv:2606.04160v2, so the counts may include that paper twice. It is still open whether arXiv:2607.08883 and https://openreview.net/forum?id=8cROPwYh3g are one work; if they are, the count of independent groups on those rows is also overstated.

source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; Oscar Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

original_result.setup: The authors ablated harmful-minus-harmless activation directions across all layers, added them at their source layers, and evaluated weight edits and capabilities.
original_result.result: Ablation reduced refusal and addition induced refusal on harmless prompts; with the default system prompt, Qwen 7B HarmBench attack success rose from 7.0% to 79.2% after weight editing. Capability losses occurred: Gemma 7B TruthfulQA accuracy fell from 47.1% to 44.7%.

wording_issues.issue: Many results reduce refusal without removing it, and in some models the intervention leaves it untouched or raises it. Residual refusal: Llama-3-8B-Instruct ASR only 10.4→53.3 (per-layer DIM directions patched to the harmless mean rather than zeroed); LLaMA-3.2-3B harmful responses 6/313→133/313 (313 StrongREJECT prompts, Llama-Guard judge; direction recipe not stated); Command-R-7B 68%→33%; Llama-3.1-70B 71%→59%; GLM-5.3-Flash 0.380 on StrongREJECT and 0.480 on SimpleSafetyTests; abliterated Llama-3.3-70B-IT unsafe-response rate only 30.48% against 7.94% aligned (GPT-4.1 judge, whose other classes include invalid, so the rest is not all refusal); fortified Mistral-SU harmfulness 0.08/0.04/0.15 (judge harmfulness scores, not refusal rates). No change or reversal: Llama-3.2-3B refusal-substring 0.7885→0.7885; Mistral-Large 0.0pp change under a domain-specific direction on ≤30% of layers (the authors say Heretic can abliterate it); Qwen3-14B 78%→94%. 'Reduces' fits many rows better than 'removes'.

At the natural magnitude, induction is absent or partial in several models, and in some settings addition lowers refusal. 1× the harmful-benign gap gives benign refusal 0.00 (Mistral-7B), 0.01 (Gemma-3-27B), 0.33 (Qwen3-14B), 0.24 (Llama-3.1-70B); in another study Llama-3.1-70B stays 1%→1%; Llama-3.1-8B at +0.5 r (layer 18) goes 1%→10% (random 0%); Llama-3.2-3B reaches only 0.55 at α=1 (baseline 0.00), against 0.95 for Llama-3.2-1B. Non-monotonic or reversed: in Qwen3-VL-4B, rescaling visual tokens' projection on an unsafe-minus-safe vision-encoder direction (h+α(h·Ê)Ê, global, layers 7–10) raises unsafe rejection 84→94% at α=1 but lowers it to 70% at α=2 and 6% at α=4, while layers 18–20 stay at 80–84% at every α; adding raises Mistral-7B roleplay attack success 63.5%→78.0%. Induction also depends on strength: Llama-3.2-1B/3B benign refusal is 0.00–0.14 at α=2–4 (baselines 0.05 and 0.00) as outputs degrade; in Qwen3-8B an added ACT-minus-base direction (not harmful-minus-harmless) gives benign refusal 0.0% at α=1, 1.0% at α=2, 0.0% at α=5 and 20.7% at α=10, and jailbreak refusal 4.1%, 6.1%, 61.2% and 100.0% at the same α (unsteered 1%).

Retention depends on the model, the selection criterion, the benchmark and the strength. Kept: MMLU/ARC-C/GSM8K within about 2.6 points in 2502.17420; MMLU degradation ≤0.028 across 24 models in 2607.02714; GSM8K 0.676→0.676 on Qwen2.5-1.5B. Not kept: gemma-3-1b-it MMLU 40.95%→0.00% (all 1,531 answers unparseable at an 8-token budget) and GSM8K 31.00%→0.00%, with the direction chosen under a loosened KL filter (threshold 10) and the induce-refusal filter off; Phi-4-Mini MMLU −22.44 and GSM8k −28.13 points; TruthfulQA falls in all seven models of 2502.17420 (e.g. 61.1→52.8); Qwen3.5-27B TruthfulQA MC2 58.25%→51.39%; refusal-only selection costs −6.0 pp MMLU on Qwen2.5-7B while joint min-KL selection stays within −0.8 to +1.0 pp; in 2610.28982 generic-prompt KL is 0.25–11.34 in Qwen3-14B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-3-27B and Llama-3.1-70B, above the original <0.1 criterion (11.34 on Gemma-3-27B under raw all-layer ablation), and Command-R-7B passes on generic prompts (0.04) but not on the benchmark's benign prompts (0.14).

wording_issues.phrase: a difference-in-means direction (harmful minus harmless instructions)
wording_issues.issue: Which difference-in-means vector you get, from which estimator and contrast, changes the result. On Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, user_end extraction selects L1 and gives 93.75%→87.5% (the README calls this direction non-causal and uses it as a negative control), while L19 last_full gives 93.75%→0%. Llama-3 needed a harmless-mean offset instead of zeroing. The harmful-minus-benign carrier fails to reopen ASR on Llama-3.1-8B (0.1675→0.1400), where a refusal-vs-compliance carrier works. Steerability of dataset-derived vectors runs from 0.990 (WildGuardMix, Tülu-3-8B) to 0.667 (Do-Not-Answer, an external dataset, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct); per model it is 0.730–0.990 on Tülu and 0.667–0.960 on Llama. On Gemma-3 the raw difference-of-means estimator gives 0 feasible cells at every size (1b 0/156, 4b 0/204, 12b 0/288, 27b 0/186), while scale-corrected estimators give usable directions. In 2606.23671 no Gemma-3 DIM candidate (4B, 12B, 27B) passed the strict (0.1) or relaxed (0.5) harmless-KL threshold, so a bypass-only direction was used (KL 5.649/1.806/0.742), and ablation still raised Gemma-3-12B ASR by +10.6. Many effective directions in the packs come from other contrasts entirely: refusal-vs-compliance, refused-minus-nonrefused, probe, ACT-minus-base, topic/category, SVD of a fine-tuning shift, SAE features.

In some models and training regimes no single direction mediates refusal, and in some settings mediation is partial. GPT-OSS-20B: the direction coherently flips 4% of refusals. After extended-refusal fine-tuning, refusal stays at 90.9–96.7%. After L1+KD training of Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, K=11 directions are needed to bring harmful refusal under a 30% threshold. That threshold was set at the unmodified Instruct model's own K=1 rate, and the K=1 rate after L1+KD is not stated. In Llama-2-13B base, ablation raises refusal 0.24→0.37. In the tool-call setting, restoring the projection reverts only 18–62% of unsafe calls. With prefill-only all-layer ablation (blinded LLM judge, Gemma 2 2B/9B and Qwen 2.5 3B/7B), harmful refusal stays at .527–.860 on XSTest (Gemma 2-2B .980→.527, Gemma 2-9B .973→.860) while WildGuardTest falls to .067–.180; the study does not describe the two benchmarks' prompt types. Removing the direction from behaviour-steering vectors cuts their |ΔASR| by only 2–25%.

The statement does not say which refusal measure it means, and the measures disagree on the same outputs. Keyword or explicit refusal can go to zero while judged compliance stays partial: Llama-2-7b-chat substring ASR 0.98 but LlamaGuard 0.54 (version given as 4 in Table 1 and as 2 in the methods) and HarmBench 0.62; Qwen2.5-3B substring refusal 1.0000→0.1731 while HarmBench reaches only 0.2019 and LlamaGuard 3 0.2212; Qwen2.5-1.5B reads 0.0 refusal by keyword and about 0.49 true compliance by an LLM judge; Qwen3.5-9B block reconstructions strip keyword refusal with judged compliance 0.00; gemma-3-1b StrongREJECT judge scores stay below 0.7 of 5; Phi-4-mini any-refusal falls only 35.3→18.6. Markers can also overcount refusal. After Heretic, a marker heuristic leaves 16–54 of 100 refusals (no pre-edit rate). But on separate generations from six abliterated models, a classifier gives 84.7–100% non-refusal against 50.0–86.7% by markers, and marker refusal precision is 11.2%. Refusal also persists as deflection: an ablated Qwen3.8-27B obeys 59/64 direct orders but only 2/32 when a hand-off tool is available.

The statement does not say how or where the ablation is applied, and that decides the outcome. On OLMo-3 a weight-folded edit (attention-out and MLP-down at layer 19) removes refusal (0.575→0.000), while single-layer projection of the same direction at layer 16 raises it (0.62→0.78). Single-layer DiM ablation reaches +0.46 non-refusal on Llama-2 against +0.91 all-layer, and +0.03/+0.06/+0.20 at INLP's layer. In an MoE, single writer groups remove 0.016–0.148 against 0.776 for all three jointly. Final-norm-hook projection gives +2.9 pp on Qwen3-4B against 36.3 pp all-layer. Single-layer projection at a peak-separation layer gives 0.14→0.14 on Llama-3.1-8B and 0.96→0.92 on Gemma-2-9B. That study does not compare sites, and the same intervention gave marked partial drops in Qwen-2.5-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.2 and SOLAR-10.7B. In LLaDA-8B-Instruct, the one diffusion LM tested, projecting only at input tokens gives a clear but incomplete reduction (the authors: the majority of the effect). Projecting only at output tokens gives little or no change, and projecting at all tokens is strongest (keyword refusal baseline 97.0; per-condition figure values cannot be placed).

Several of the strongest removals use one direction per layer or several directions, and in some models one direction is reported as insufficient. The strongest MoE and Heretic results tune per-layer, per-component weights. Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B goes 11/12→9/12 refusals with one global direction and to 0/12 with per-layer directions on all 40 layers (12 prompts, marker-list judge). In Gemma-7B-it, one direction lifts compliance from 37.9% to 75.0% and a second to 83.2%. A third and fourth add 0.3 and 1.3 points, inside about 3 points of noise, and the author calls the refusal plane two-dimensional. After L1+KD fine-tuning of Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, K=11 directions are needed to bring harmful refusal under a 30% threshold. That threshold was set at the unmodified Instruct model's own K=1 rate, and the K=1 rate after L1+KD is not stated. On Qwen3 8B/14B, the authors report single-direction ablation as insufficient regardless of extraction method.

The result changes with where the contrast is read and which prompts form it, and some effective directions are taken outside the instruction positions. In MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B, a prompt-final-token direction left refusal unchanged across every variant tried, while a response-region direction cut it 78.1%→9.4% (Variant D; Variant C 40.6%). In reasoning models the better token position depends on the model. On a 24-prompt held-out subset, a CoT-token direction gives mean StrongREJECT compliance 0.888 against 0.294 for an end-of-prompt direction on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B. But end-of-prompt is higher on Qwen-7B (0.819 vs 0.713 CoT), Qwen3-8B (0.604 vs 0.498) and GPT-OSS-20B (0.562 vs 0.519), and leaves 4.1–10.1% refusal on n=487. Both directions are refused-minus-complied, not harmful-minus-harmless. The harmless set also matters. Qwen2.5-Omni-7B's L16 direction is fit at the last chat-templated prompt position. Refitting it with natural XSTest benign prompts instead of templated domain-matched hard negatives shrinks ΔG from −7.10 to −1.79 [−1.88, −1.70]. That is below the study's 3.55 band threshold, though still far larger than L08's −0.03, and random directions leave G unchanged.

wording_issues.phrase: mediates refusal: ablating it removes refusal, adding it induces refusal
wording_issues.issue: The statement implies both halves hold in the same model, which several studies do not find. In Gemma-1.1-7B-IT ablation works, but ActAdd leaves refusal at 0.36–0.41 and induces harmless refusal only to 0.62. In Qwen3-32B, adding the L58 refused-minus-nonrefused direction (a refused-vs-answered split, not harmful-minus-harmless) raises benign refusal 5%→93% at the selection stage. Removing it moves diagnostic harmful refusal 2%→7%, and the authors find no evidence the direction is necessary. Every-layer abliteration of that vector removes 12.8 pp of 400 held-out over-refusals; a separate paired rewrite-displacement direction removes 36.8 pp. In Olmo 3 7B Instruct (layer 15, LLM judge, baseline about 31%), positive steering drives refusal 'very high, sometimes near-total'. Single-layer negative steering (coefficients −1 to −2) gives only modest reductions below baseline. Ablation is not tested, and the source checkpoint of the directions is not stated. In Llama-3.1-8B-SFT, ablation leaves 0.99→0.79 while addition reaches 0.01→1.0. In Llama-3.1-8B base, addition reaches 0.59 while ablation moves a low baseline 0.21→0.17.

method_sensitivity.factor: Extraction layer and token position of the direction
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, refusal rate by extraction layer (gh:mbkaleb): layers 2–5, 7–9 and 12 leave refusal at 1.00; layers 11, 13, 17 and 18 give 0.69, 0.81, 0.19 and 0.44; layers 14–16 and 19–27 give 0.00. The canonical user_end extraction selects L1 and moves refusal only 93.75%→87.5%, against 93.75%→0% for L19 last_full. The README calls the L1 direction non-causal and later uses it as a negative control. Qwen3.8-27B validation refusal is 0% at layers 37 and 41, 36% at layer 53 and 70% at layer 56. Llama-3-8B-Instruct: direct-ablation ASR ranges from 0% to 100% across layer choices and the study's own vector-calculation variants.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention site and scope (all-layer vs single-layer, weight fold vs activation, writer groups, final-norm hook)
method_sensitivity.what: Single-layer DiM ablation reaches +0.46 non-refusal on Llama-2 7B against +0.91 all-layer, and collapses to +0.03 (Qwen), +0.06 (Llama-2) and +0.20 (Llama-3) at INLP's layer. On OLMo-3 a weight-folded edit gives 0.575→0.000 while single-layer projection of the same direction raises refusal 0.62→0.78. On GLM-5.3-Flash MoE, single writer groups remove 0.016–0.148 and all three jointly 0.776; layer-boundary projection leaves 0.265 against 0.174 for the writer edit. Projecting at the final-norm hook gives Qwen3-4B +2.9 pp against 36.3 pp with all-layer ablation, and gemma-2-2b-it +2.1 pp. Projecting the Arditi direction at one peak-separation layer gives no drop on Llama-3.1-8B (0.14→0.14) or Gemma-2-9B (0.96→0.92).

method_sensitivity.factor: Refusal judge or measure (substring/keyword vs classifier or LLM judge)
method_sensitivity.what: After ablation, JailbreakBench ASR is 95–100% by substring and 82–83% by LlamaGuard2 (Gemma-2-2B-IT 8%→97% vs 2%→83%). Llama-2-7b-chat ablation: substring ASR 0.39→0.98, LlamaGuard 4 0.00→0.54, HarmBench 0.00→0.62. Qwen2.5-3B ablation: substring refusal 1.0→0.1731 but HarmBench 0.0→0.2019 and LlamaGuard 3 0→0.2212. Phi-4-mini explicit refusal is removed while any-refusal falls only 35.3→18.6, 37.4→14.1 and 39.9→10.1. The same Qwen2.5-1.5B ablation run reads 0.0 refusal by keyword but about 0.49 true compliance by an LLM judge. The same alpha=1.0 Basic RD edit on Qwen3-8B-Base scores ASR 0.22 (WildGuard), 0.11 (Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B) and 0.44 (Llama-Guard-3-8B).

Refusal-only selection costs MMLU −6.0 pp on Qwen2.5-7B (college CS 68.0%→56.0%), −3.8 pp on Llama-3.1-8B and −0.7 pp on Mistral. Joint min-KL selection gives aggregate MMLU changes of +0.1 (Qwen), 0.0 (Llama) and −0.6 pp (Mistral). Under a KL≤0.1 filter no DIM direction passes on Gemma-2-2B, while the affine ACE variant does (+53.1 ASR). Without the filter, DIM gives +63.7 ASR with large side effects (TruthfulQA −19.0, ARC-C −6.0). Gemma-3 fails both KL thresholds (harmless KL 5.649 on 4B, 1.8 on 12B, 0.74 on 27B) and uses bypass-only selection. Ablation then raises Gemma-3-12B ASR by only +10.6 (Llama Guard 3 1B, figure labels), while Gemma-3-27B's ASR rises substantially. Gemma-2-27B: fluency-gated layer selection gives HarmBench ASR 0.56, while refusal-only selection gives ASR 0.00 with benign perplexity 8.0×10⁶, i.e. a destroyed model.

method_sensitivity.factor: Direction estimator and contrast data (raw vs scaled/masked/purified; which harmful and harmless sets)
method_sensitivity.what: Gemma-3-12B: the raw estimator yields no feasible candidate and raw ablation drives MMLU 0.682→0.242, while masked/standardized/winsorized estimators reach refusal 0.000–0.053. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: a Gram-Schmidt-purified direction leaves 28.8% refusal against 43.2% raw (from about 96.0%). Gemma 4 E4B-it: standard rank-1 abliteration leaves should_refuse at the base rate of 100% (base measured on the GGUF/llama.cpp path), against 40.5% (α=1.0, n=42) for a chat-template + winsorization + Gram-Schmidt variant; the README credits the Gram-Schmidt step. Steerability S of difference-of-means vectors from different datasets runs from 0.990 (WildGuardMix, Tülu-3-8B) to 0.667 (Do-Not-Answer, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct a Min-K%++ top-128 subset gives 0.489 against 0.943 for random subsets. On Tülu-3-8B the same selection gives 0.974 against 0.966.

Llama-3.2-1B benign refusal under addition rises from 0.05 (baseline) to 0.89 at α=0.5 and 0.95 at α=1, and is 0.00 at α=2 and 4 (gibberish). Llama-3.2-3B, from 0.00, gives 0.36, 0.55, 0.14 and 0.00 (keyword matcher, 64-prompt held-out split). Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (n=8 illicit prompts, substring classifier): the illicit response rate is 37.5% at α=0 and still 37.5% at α=1.0 (exact ablation, perplexity 1.03x). It is 87.5% at α=2.0, and perplexity is 530,115x baseline at α=3.0 (token soup). Llama-2-7B-Chat, steering at layers 10–17: ASR 1% at α=0, 4% (α=−0.05), 45% (−0.15), 94% (−0.20), 97% (−0.25, 19% degenerate). GLM-5.3-Flash refusal is 62.5 / 41.7 / 33.3 / 41.7 / 62.5% at λ = 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 / 1.75 / 2.0, and reads 0% at λ=2.5 only because output is empty.

method_sensitivity.factor: Direction variant and intervention form (zeroing vs harmless-mean offset, affine, mean-out, gated, rotation, subtraction vs projection)
method_sensitivity.what: Llama-3: zeroing the direction degraded the model (unquantified), so arXiv:2409.20089 instead patches per-layer DIM directions to the mean harmless projection at the last user-turn token. Affine (ACE) ablation of the same direction gives +58.9 (Llama-3.1-8B) and +60.4 (Qwen-2.5-7B) ASR points, against +73.1 and +72.7 for DIM. ACE acts at the selected layer only and DIM at all layers. Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: a manifold-projected direction gives 100% JSR against 74% for the unprojected baseline at α=2.0. Gemma-4-E4B-IT, StrongREJECT: gated restoration of the study's own hidden-state DIM direction (layers at 40–85% depth) gives 82.7%→0.0% under fixed prefill and 92.3%→1.6% under deep prefill. Unconditional addition of the Arditi-pipeline vector at one layer (α=0.5) gives 82.7%→85.6% and 92.3%→93.9%. The two directions are built differently, and random directions with J-Anchor's gate also reach 0.3%.

method_sensitivity.factor: Prompt set, category and language (of evaluation prompts or direction source)
method_sensitivity.what: GLM-5.3-Flash edited refusal is 0.131 on AdvBench but 0.380 on StrongREJECT and 0.480 on SimpleSafetyTests, and stays 0.48–0.62 in violence, sexual content and hate. Prefill-only all-layer ablation (blinded gemini-3.7-flash judge) leaves harmful refusal at .527–.860 on XSTest against .067–.180 on WildGuardTest (Gemma 2 2B/9B, Qwen 2.5 3B/7B). vi-smollm-135m, one weight edit (layer-23 direction), strict regex refusal, n=100 per set: 92%→12% (long harmful), 69%→5% (short), 94%→28% (command). Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, compliance on Bashkir and Tajik prompts: ablating each language's own direction gives 87.9%→0.722 and 92.0%→0.920 (fraction after ablation). Ablating the English direction gives 0.977 and 0.991 on the same prompts (English prompts: 4.9%→0.998).

After single-layer ActAdd subtraction, GPT-OSS 20B ASR is 0.94 with no system prompt, 0.66 with a lightweight refusal prompt and 0.83 with the Llama-2 prompt; Mixtral 8x7B gives 0.92, 0.77 and 0.77 and OLMoE 0.90, 0.94, 0.93. Under graded ablation from a fixed layer, tool-mediated refusal breaks at a lower dose than conversational refusal in Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B, Llama-3.1-70B, Ministral-3-8B, Gemma-4-12B and Gemma-4-31B. Restoring a tool run's refusal-direction projection to its no-tool value reverts 18% (Qwen3-14B), 24% (Mistral-7B), 62% (Command-R-7B), 46% (Gemma-3-27B) and 40% (Llama-3.1-70B) of unsafe tool calls to safe. arXiv:2607.02396's problems line says LLM-judge evaluation is sensitive to system prompts.

method_sensitivity.factor: Thinking mode, reasoning tuning and chain-of-thought handling
method_sensitivity.what: GLM-4.7-Flash with thinking enabled clears all held-out probes (10/10→0/10), while with thinking disabled 1/10 residual remains. The two runs use different directions (layer 29 trace-closing token vs layer 19 final template position). Qwen3.5-4B keeps 1/6 Target-Semantic and 1/10 held-out probes with thinking off. Weight orthogonalization on the reasoning-tuned checkpoint Qwen3-4B* gives StrongREJECT 81.2%→70.6%, against 99.4%→38.7% on instruction-tuned Qwen3-4B (separate Thinking-2507 and Instruct-2507 checkpoints). DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B: steering along the EOI direction reaches 39% compliance with the original CoT, 70% with the CoT suppressed and 94% with the CoT regenerated. Refused-minus-complied directions, n=24 held-out prompts, mean StrongREJECT compliance: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B gives 0.888 (CoT-token direction) against 0.294 (end-of-prompt). GPT-OSS-20B gives 0.519 against 0.562, and 39.9% of its end-of-prompt generations are incomplete.
